study_material.title: Probability - Complete Study Notes
study_material.introduction: Probability = favourable outcomes / total outcomes, ranging from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain). Placement questions live on dice, coins, cards and coloured balls - master the sample spaces and the rest is counting.
learning_objectives: Compute probabilities from equally likely sample spaces
Use the addition rule and complements
Apply the multiplication rule for independent and dependent events
Solve dice, coin, card and ball-drawing problems

concepts.heading: 1. Sample Spaces
concepts.body: One die: 6 outcomes. Two dice: 36 ordered pairs. One coin: 2; n coins: 2^n. A deck: 52 cards, 4 suits of 13, 26 red and 26 black, 12 face cards (J,Q,K in each suit), 4 aces. Know these cold.

concepts.heading: 2. Basic Rule and Complement
concepts.body: P(E) = favourable/total when outcomes are equally likely. P(not E) = 1 - P(E). 'At least one' is nearly always fastest via the complement: P(at least one head in 2 tosses) = 1 - P(no head) = 1 - 1/4 = 3/4.

concepts.heading: 3. Addition Rule
concepts.body: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B). For mutually exclusive events the overlap is zero. Example: P(king or queen) = 4/52 + 4/52 = 2/13.

concepts.heading: 4. Multiplication Rule
concepts.body: Independent events: P(A and B) = P(A) x P(B). Without replacement, probabilities change: P(two aces) = 4/52 x 3/51 = 1/221. Always ask whether the first draw affects the second.

concepts.heading: 5. Classic Setups
concepts.body: Two dice sums: 7 is most likely (6 ways, P = 1/6). Leap year has 366 days = 52 weeks + 2 days; P(53 Sundays) = 2/7. Balls from a bag: use combinations - P(both red from 4R 3B) = 4C2/7C2 = 6/21 = 2/7.

formulas: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B)
shortcut_methods: Two-dice questions: memorise counts of each sum (2:1 way ... 7:6 ways ... 12:1 way)
common_mistakes: Forgetting to subtract the overlap in the addition rule
Treating draws without replacement as independent
Counting 2-dice outcomes as 21 instead of 36 (order matters in the sample space)
study_material.summary: Count the sample space, count the favourable cases, and reach for complements on 'at least' questions.
